nodes.name: Ni(OH)2 electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: Ni(OH)2 nanosheets were grown on cleaned NF through a simple electrodeposition method. Typically, the deposition was executed in a typical three-electrode setup comprising of NF as the working electrode, a graphite rod as the counter electrode, and an Ag/AgCl (saturated KCl solution) as the reference electrode, respectively. The potentiostatic deposition was then performed at -0.95 V versus Ag/AgCl in 40×10^-3 M Ni(NO3)2·6H2O electrolyte bath at 85 °C for 1000 s. After that, the as-deposited Ni(OH)2 nanosheets electrode was carefully removed and rinsed with water and ethanol, then dried in a vacuum oven.
nodes.source_text: Synthesis of Ni(OH)2 Nanosheets: Ni(OH)2 nanosheets were grown on cleaned NF through a simple electrodeposition method... dried in a vacuum oven.

nodes.name: NiSe2 solvothermal selenization
nodes.procedure: The as-obtained Ni(OH)2 electrode was converted into NiSe2 via a solvothermal selenization method. Specially, 0.296 g Se power was dissolved in 25 mL dimethylformamide, 0.5 mL n-butylamine, and 0.15 mL hydrazine to form a mixed solution under vigorously stirring. The above solution together with the Ni(OH)2 nanosheets electrode were transferred to a 50 mL Teflon-lined stainless steel container and heated at 180 °C for 1 h. After cooling to room temperature, the octahedral-like NiSe2 was obtained.

nodes.name: Ce-modified Ni(OH)2 electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: The Ce·m·Ni(OH)2@NiSe2 electrode was synthesized by growing ultrathin nanoflower-like Ce-m-Ni(OH)2 on the NiSe2 scaffold via potentiostatic electrodeposition at -0.85 V vs Ag/AgCl in electrolyte containing 36×10^-3 M Ni(NO3)2·6H2O, 4×10^-3 M Ce(NO3)3·6H2O, and 0.75 M urea at 85 °C for 800 s. Comparative samples Ni(OH)2@NiSe2, Ce(OH)3@NiSe2, and different Ce content variants (2%, 5%, 15% molar ratios) were prepared using similar procedure without Ce(NO3)3·6H2O, without Ni(NO3)2·6H2O, or by tuning Ce(NO3)3/[Ni+Ce] molar ratios to ~0.02, 0.05, 0.15 respectively.
nodes.source_text: Synthesis of the Ce-m-Ni(OH)2@NiSe2 Electrode: The Ce·m·Ni(OH)2@NiSe2 electrode was synthesized... for 800 s. For comparisons, the samples of Ce(OH)3@NiSe2 and Ni(OH)2@NiSe2 were also prepared... three control electrodes were also fabricated by modulating the molar ratios...

nodes.description: OER performance in O₂-saturated 1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: The electrocatalytic performance of the Ce-m-Ni(OH)₂@NiSe₂ electrode toward OER was measured in O₂-saturated 1 M KOH solution by using a typical three-electrode configuration... overpotential of 158 mV at 10 mA cm⁻²... Tafel slope of 27 mV dec⁻¹... Faradaic efficiency of 98%... no obvious decay at 50 mA cm⁻² for 20 h
the Ce⋅m⋅Ni(OH)₂@NiSe₂ electrode exhibits an impressive OER activity with an overpotential of 158 mV at a current density of 10 mA cm⁻², which is much smaller than those of Ni(OH)₂@NiSe₂ (225 mV)

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns show characteristic peaks of cubic NiSe2 (JCPDS No. 88-1711), β-Ni(OH)2 (JCPDS No. 14-0117 at 19.2°, 33.1°, 39.0°, 60.1°, 70.2°), and Ce(OH)3 (JCPDS No. 74-0665 at 28.3°, 48.6°, 70.3°, 71.4°).
nodes.evidence_snippet: After the electrodeposition of Ce·m·Ni(OH)2 on the surface of NiSe2, two new sets of diffraction peaks in Ce-m-Ni(OH)2 appear (see Figure 2a), which are ascribed to βNi(OH)2 and Ce(OH)3 phases.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows Ni-O-Ce bonds at 613 cm⁻¹ indicating Ce doping into Ni(OH)2, and broad band at 494-568 cm⁻¹ indicative of oxygen vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As presented in Figure 2b and Figure S5 in the Supporting Information, the existence of Ni-O-Ce bonds at about 613 cm⁻¹ further reveals that partial Ce was doped into Ni(OH)2...

nodes.characterization_summary: BET surface area of Ce-m-Ni(OH)2@NiSe2 with NF substrate is 20 m²/g; peeled powder sample shows 51 m²/g (2.5x higher). Mesopores at ≈3.7 nm and ≈13.1 nm by BJH method.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From Figure 2c, the BET surface area of Ce-m-Ni(OH)2@NiSe2 is relatively small (only 20 m² g⁻¹) since the NF substrate is included... As shown in Figure S6... the BET surface areas of the Ce-m-Ni(OH)2@NiSe2 powder is 51 m² g⁻¹, which is about 2.5 times as high as that of the Ce·m·Ni(OH)2@NiSe2 sample with the NF substrate.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows nanoflower-like Ce-m-Ni(OH)2 composed of interconnected ultrathin nanosheets (4-8 nm thickness) with open porous structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Closer observations (see Figure S8, Supporting Information, and Figure 2d,e) found that the nanoflower-like Ce·m·Ni(OH)2 was composed of interconnected ultrathin nanosheets (about 4-8 nm in thickness size).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice distances: 0.231 nm for (002) Ni(OH)2, 0.211 nm and 0.344 nm for (220)/(111) NiSe2, 0.324 nm for (110) Ce(OH)3.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2f shows a high-resolution TEM image of Ce·m·Ni(OH)2@NiSe2. Thereinto, the lattice distance of 0.231 nm is indexed to (002) plane of Ni(OH)2.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX mappings show uniform distribution of Ni, Ce, O elements; Se mainly on internal space.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2g–k shows a scanning TEM image and the corresponding energy-dispersive X-ray spectrum (EDX) mappings of Ce-m-Ni(OH)2@NiSe2, revealing the uniform distribution of Ni, Ce, and O elements...

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows Ni 2p3/2 at 853.2 eV (Ni-Se), 855.3 eV (Ni oxidation); Se 3d at 55.0 eV (Ni-Se), 59.1 eV (Se-O); Ce 3d with Ce³⁺ (peaks 1,3,7,10) and Ce⁴⁺ (peaks 2,4-6,8,9,11,12).
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the Ni 2p3/2 spectrum in Figure 3b, the sharp peak at about 853.2 eV... is assigned to characteristic peak of Ni-Se. While the two broad peaks at 855.3 and 861.4 eV are attributed to the Ni oxidation...

nodes.characterization_summary: Actual Ce contents: 4.5 at% (2%Ce-doped), 8.1 at% (5%Ce-m-), 14.0 at% (Ce-m-), 20.7 at% (15%Ce-m-Ni(OH)2@NiSe2).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The actual Ce contents were 4.5, 8.1, 14.0, and 20.7 at%, respectively, for 2%Ce-doped Ni(OH)2@NiSe2, 5%Ce-m-Ni(OH)2@NiSe2, Ce-m-Ni(OH)2@NiSe2 and 15%Ce-m-Ni(OH)2@NiSe2, identified by inductively coupled plasma-optical emission spectroscopy (ICP-OES).

nodes.characterization_summary: Double-layer capacitance Cdl = 5.1 mF cm⁻² indicates ECSA for Ce-m-Ni(OH)2@NiSe2 (vs Ni(OH)2@NiSe2: 5.7 mF cm⁻², Ce(OH)3@NiSe2: 2.1 mF cm⁻²). NiSe2 support Cdl = 1.5 mF cm⁻² vs NF 0.3 mF cm⁻².
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ce·m·Ni(OH)2@NiSe2 electrode has a larger Cdl value of 5.1 mF cm⁻² than that of Ce(OH)3@NiSe2 (2.1 mF cm⁻²) and even comparable to that of Ni(OH)2@NiSe2 (5.7 mF cm⁻²), suggesting more accessible active sites.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows Rs = 0.7 Ω, Rct = 1.4 Ω for Ce-m-Ni(OH)2@NiSe2 (vs Ni(OH)2@NiSe2: Rs=0.8Ω, Rct=2.8Ω; Ce(OH)3@NiSe2: Rs=1.1Ω, Rct=3.1Ω).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ce·m·Ni(OH)2@NiSe2 electrode shows smaller solution resistance (Rs = 0.7 Ω) and charge transfer resistance (Rct = 1.4 Ω) relative to Ni(OH)2@NiSe2 (Rs = 0.8 Ω, Rct = 2.8 Ω)...

nodes.characterization_summary: EELS shows O K-edge peaks, Ni L3/L2 edges at 854/870 eV (Ni²⁺), Ce M5/M4/post-edge peaks at ≈882/900/907 eV indicating Ce³⁺ and Ce⁴⁺ coexistence.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the low energy-loss region, three peaks can be assigned to the typical oxygen K edges. Two peaks at 854 and 870 eV are assigned to the feature of L3 and L2 edge, respectively, of Ni²⁺. In the high energy-loss region, the M5 (≈882 eV), M4 (≈900 eV), and postedge (≈907 eV) peaks indicate the coexistence of Ce³⁺ and Ce⁴⁺.
